chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife before he performed the Tawaf al-Nisa', and he said: 'Upon him is a fat camel.'
I said: A man kissed his wife, and he had performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' but she had not performed it, and he said: 'Upon him is blood (damm) which he must shed from himself.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.جَزُورٌ: A fat camel, used here as a specific measure of expiation
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to the sacrifice of an animal (usually a sheep) in the context of Hajj expiation
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed by women to complete Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife before she completes Tawaf al-Nisa'?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the distinction between major and minor sexual acts during Hajj, assigning a heavier expiation (a fat camel) for full intercourse before the wife’s Tawaf al-Nisa', and a lighter one (a sheep) for mere kissing. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the wife’s completion of Tawaf al-Nisa' is a condition for the permissibility of marital relations, linking the penalty directly to the specific ritual stage missed. This underscores the precision required in observing Hajj conditions, where the nature of the act determines the severity of the compensation.
